reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific mechanistic claims about dislocation behavior, stress concentration, and fracture in CoCrFeMnNi, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the strain-rate-dependent dislocation dynamics or fracture mechanisms specific to this HEA, so the lack of cited support leaves all key premises ungrounded.
premises: Dislocation generation rate exceeds mobility at high strain rates in CoCrFeMnNi
Dislocation pile-ups create stress concentrations that trigger micro-crack initiation along slip bands
High strain rate reduces toughness relative to quasi-static loading in this HEA
Dislocation pile-up is the primary driver of brittle fracture, distinguishable from twinning or amorphous bands
In-situ SEM/DIC and TEM can spatially correlate pile-ups with crack initiation
